ἔργων. Τουτέστι τὸ πληρωθῆναι οἴκους ἀγαθῶν. Στίχ. ιθʹ. Ἄμεμπτος δὲ ἐμυκτήρισεν
αὐτούς. Τίνας; ἢ τὴν βουλὴν τῶν ἀσεβῶν; Οἷον· βούλονταί τινα διδάσκειν τὰ
ἐναντία τῇ ἀληθείᾳ, ἐν τῷ λέ γειν· ἃ λέγουσι δόγματα μοχθηρὰ ἔχοντες. Ταῦτα
ἄμεμπτος ὁρῶν μυκτηρίζει. Στίχ. κʹ. Καὶ τὸ κατάλειμμα αὐτῶν καταφάγεται πῦρ. Τοῦ
αὐτοῦ. Τοῦτο ὃ καταλέλειπται κατὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς, τῶν προτέρων ἀποθανόντων, τὸ
πῦρ κατα φάγεται. Στίχ. κβʹ. Ἔλαβε δὲ ἐκ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἐξηγο ρίαν. Τὴν ἐξηγορίαν
ἐζήτουν κατ' ἐμαυτὸν, τί σημαίνει. Καὶ εὗρον ἐν ἄλλῃ ἐκδόσει ἀντ' αὐτῆς
ἐξομολόγησιν· Φησὶν οὖν μᾶλλον· Ἐξομολόγησαι περὶ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων σου·
ἔκλαβε ἀπὸ τοῦ στόματος τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσηγορίαν σὺν ἐξομολογήσει· ἀνάλαβε δὲ τὰ
ῥήματα αὐτοῦ ἐκ καρδίας σου. Ταῦτα δὲ ἔλεγεν ὁ Ἐλιφὰζ, νουθετῶν, ὡς ᾤετο, τὸν
Ἰώβ. Στίχ. κγʹ. Ἐὰν δὲ ἐπιστραφῇς, καὶ ταπεινώσῃς σεαυτὸν ἔναντι Κυρίου. Νουθετεῖ
αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸ ἐπιστρέψαι, οἰόμενος αὐ τὸν ταῦτα ἡμαρτηκότα πεπονθέναι. Στίχ. κδʹ.
Καὶ ὡς πέτρα χειμάῤῥου Σωφείρ. Ἐκ τοῦ τόπου οὗ γίνεται τὸ χρυσίον, ἐλεύσεται ἐπὶ
σὲ, οἱονεὶ, ἔσται λόγος σου ποικίλος καὶ καλός. Στίχ. κεʹ. Ἔσται οὖν σοι ὁ
Παντοκράτωρ βοηθὸς ἀπὸ ἐχθρῶν. Ἐὰν ὑποτάξῃς ἑαυτὸν, ἐὰν ἐξομολογήσῃ. 17.88
Στίχ. κεʹ. Καθαρὸν δὲ ἀποδώσει σε ὥσπερ ἀργύ ριον πεπυρωμένον. Ὑγιὲς δόγμα ......
πεπυρωμένον, ὁ Θεός. Στίχ. κ ʹ. Εἶτα παῤῥησιασθήσῃ ἐνώπιον Κυρίου. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ.
Ἐὰν ταπεινώσῃς σαυτὸν, ὑπομένῃς τὰ συμβεβηκότα, παῤῥησιασθήσῃ ἐνώπιον
Κυρίου, παῤῥησίαν ἕξεις, ὡς ἀποθέμενος τὰ ἁμαρτήματα. Στίχ. κηʹ. Ἐπὶ τῶν ὁδῶν
σου ἔσται φῶς. Τοῦ αὐτοῦ. Ἐὰν τηρήσῃς νουθεσίαν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ, καὶ ἐπιστρέψῃς καὶ
ἐξομολογήσῃ. Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν πρὸς Ἰὼβ ἐλέγετο· οὐ δικαίως δὲ ἐλέγετο· οὐ γὰρ
ἥμαρτε. Πρὸς ἡμᾶς δὲ ἐὰν λέγηται, δικαίως λέγεται. Στίχ. κηʹ. Ἀποκαταστήσῃ δέ σοι
δίαιταν δικαιοσύνης. Καὶ ἁπλῶς εἰπεῖν· Ἅπασάν σοι, φησὶ, τὴν ἁρμό ζουσαν δικαίῳ
πράξει διαμονὴν, ὥστε σε λαμπρὰς καὶ ἐπιδόξους ἔχειν τὰς πράξεις. ΚΕΦ. ΚΓʹ. Στίχ.
βʹ. Ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖα γέγονεν ἐπ' ἐμῷ στεναγμῷ. Εἰ δὲ ἐνῆν, φησὶ, παραυτὰ τῶν
τιμωριῶν τὴν ψῆφον φέρεσθαι, ἦν εὑρεῖν αὐτόν. Εἴθε ἐνῆν δικάσασθαι, φησὶ, καὶ
ἐντυχεῖν αὐτοῦ, καὶ μαθεῖν, τίνα ἦν ἃ ἤμελλέ μοι πρὸς ταῦτα ἐρεῖν, ἃ ἤμελλον
λέγειν. Ὁρᾷς πῶς ἐπέτυχεν ὅπερ ηὔχετο; Τοῦτο γὰρ ἔσχατον γέγονεν ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ.
Ἤθελον μαθεῖν τί μοι ἤμελλεν ἐρεῖν, καὶ εἰ ἔμελλέ μοι ὁμοίως κο λάζειν. Ταῦτα δὲ
εἶπον, οὐχ ὡς καταγινώσκων ἀδι κίαν. ΚΕΦ. Κ∆ʹ. Στίχ. ʹ. Ἡδύνθη αὐτῶν ἄρτος εἰς
νεωτέ ρους. Ἡδὺ, φησὶ, τοῖς ἀσεβέσι τὸ τρέφειν νεανίσκους, ἐφ' ᾧ δύνασθαι δι'
αὐτῶν τὰς ἐπηρείας ἐργάζε σθαι. ΚΕΦ. ΚΖʹ. Στίχ. βʹ. Ζῇ Κύριος, ὃς οὕτω με ἔκρινε.
Ἔλαβεν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ Ἰὼβ ὁ διάβολος, καὶ ἤτασεν αὐτὸν νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας,
πρότερον διὰ τῶν ἐκτὸς, ὕστερον δι' αὐτοῦ τοῦ σώματος, μετὰ ταῦτα καὶ διὰ τῶν
φίλων. Ὅτε γὰρ αὐτὸ ἐδοκίμασε διὰ τῆς γυναικὸς, καὶ οὐ νενίκηται ὁ Ἰὼβ, τρεῖς
φίλους ἤνεγ κεν ὁ διάβολος, οὐκ ἐχθροὺς, οὐκ ἐπίβουλα δόγματα ἔχοντας, ἀλλ'
ἀληθείας μὲν λόγους, οὐ καλῶς δὲ, οὐδὲ ἐν καιρῷ προφερομένους. Καὶ ἐβουλεύετο ὁ
διά βολος διὰ τῶν φίλων τούτων ποιῆσαι τὸν Ἰὼβ φθέγ ξασθαί τι κατὰ τῆς
Προνοίας, ἀσεβῆσαι διὰ τοὺς πόνους, ἐκκακῆσαι διὰ τὰς ἀλγηδόνας. Ἀλλ' ὁ ἀλη θῶς
ἀνδρεῖος, ὁ καρτερικὸς, ὅρα τί λέγει μετὰ τοὺς λόγους τῶν τριῶν. Ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ
Ἐλιφὰζ τρεῖς διαλέξεις, ὁ Σωφὰρ δύο διαλέξεις· τούτων γὰρ τετελεσμένων,
σιωπησάντων ἐκείνων, ὅρα τί ἀποκρί νεται μετὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἀπ' αὐτοῦ προοίμιον,
οὕτως 17.89 ἀπὸ τῆς Γραφῆς ὠνομασμένον. Τί ἀποκρίνεται; πρόσχωμεν τῇ λέξει.
Στίχ. αʹ. Ἔτι δὲ προσθεὶς ὁ Ἰὼβ εἶπε τῷ προ οιμίῳ· Στίχ. βʹ. Ζῇ Κύριος, ὃς οὕτω με
κέκρικε, καὶ ὁ Παντοκράτωρ, ὁ παραπικράνας μου ψυ χὴν, καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. Οἶδα πόθεν
pass_a_gloss: works. That is, the filling of houses with good things. Verse 19: And a blameless one sneered at them. Whom? Or the counsel of the impious? As: they want to teach someone the things opposite to the truth, in saying what they say, having wretched doctrines. Seeing these things a blameless one sneers. Verse 20: And fire will eat their remnant. Of the same. This which has been left according to the impious, the former ones having died, the fire will eat. Verse 22: And he took from his mouth an exposition. I sought the exposition by myself, what it signifies. And I found in another edition instead of it confession; so he says rather: Confess about your sins; take from the mouth of God an introduction with confession; and take up his words from your heart. And Eliphaz said these things, admonishing, as he thought, Job. Verse 23: And if you turn and humble yourself before the Lord. He admonishes him toward turning, thinking that he has suffered these things having sinned. Verse 24: And as a rock of a winter-torrent of Ophir. From the place where gold comes to be, it will come upon you — as it were, your word will be varied and beautiful. Verse 25: So the Almighty will be a helper for you from enemies. If you subject yourself, if you confess. 17.88 Verse 25: And he will render you pure as silver fired. A sound doctrine …… fired, God. Verse: Then you will speak freely before the Lord. Of the same. If you humble yourself, endure the things that have happened, you will speak freely before the Lord; you will have freedom of speech, as having put away the sins. Verse 28: Upon your ways there will be light. Of the same. If you keep admonition from me, and turn and confess. So these things were said toward Job; but they were not said justly; for he did not sin. But toward us if they are said, they are said justly. Verse 28: And he will restore to you a way of life of righteousness. And to speak simply: All the continuance fitting a righteous practice, he says, so that you have bright and glorious deeds. Chapter 23 verse 2: His hand has become heavy upon my groan. And if it were possible, he says, for the vote of the punishments to be brought at once, it was possible to find him. Would that it were possible to go to court, he says, and to petition him, and to learn what things he was going to say to me toward these things which I was going to say. Do you see how he obtained what he prayed? For this has happened last in the book. I wanted to learn what he was going to say to me, and whether he was going to punish me likewise. And I said these things, not as condemning injustice. Chapter 24 verse: Their bread was sweetened unto younger ones. Sweet, he says, to the impious is to feed young men, upon which to be able through them to work the insults. Chapter 27 verse 2: The Lord lives, who has thus judged me. The devil received authority over Job, and tested him night and day, first through the outward things, later through the body itself, after these also through the friends. For when he tested him through the wife, and Job was not conquered, the devil brought three friends — not enemies, not having plotting doctrines, but words of truth, yet not well, nor brought forward in season. And the devil planned through these friends to make Job utter something against Providence, to be impious because of the toils, to grow weary because of the pains. But the truly courageous, the enduring one — see what he says after the words of the three. When Eliphaz finished three dialogues, Sophar two dialogues; these having been finished, those having fallen silent, see what he answers after the preface said from him, thus 17.89 named from Scripture. What does he answer? Let us attend to the wording. Verse 1: And Job still adding said to the preface: Verse 2: The Lord lives, who has thus judged me, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul, and the rest. I know from where
pass_b_english: works — that is, houses filled with goods. "[[A blameless one sneered at them >> Bible:Job 22:19]]" — at the counsel of the impious who teach opposite the truth with wretched doctrines. "[[Fire will eat their remnant >> Bible:Job 22:20]]." "[[He took from his mouth an exposition >> Bible:Job 22:22]]:" Origen found another edition reading confession — Confess your sins; take from God’s mouth an introduction with confession; take up his words from your heart. Eliphaz said this thinking he admonished Job. "[[If you turn and humble yourself before the Lord >> Bible:Job 22:23]]." "[[As a rock of a winter-torrent of Ophir >> Bible:Job 22:24]]:" from the gold-place your word will come varied and beautiful. "[[The Almighty will be a helper from enemies >> Bible:Job 22:25]]" if you subject yourself and confess. "[[He will render you pure as fired silver >> Bible:Job 22:25]]." Then free speech before the Lord, sins put away. "[[Upon your ways there will be light >> Bible:Job 22:28]]; he will restore a way of life of righteousness." Said toward Job unjustly — he did not sin — but toward us, justly.

Chapter 23: "[[His hand has become heavy upon my groan >> Bible:Job 23:2]]." If the vote of punishments could be brought at once, he could find him. Would that he could go to court, petition, and learn what God would say to what Job would say. See how he obtained what he prayed — it comes last in the book. He wanted to know the answer, and whether punishment would continue; he said this not as condemning injustice.

Chapter 24: bread sweetened for younger ones — sweet to the impious to feed young men so as to work insults through them. Chapter 27: "[[The Lord lives, who has thus judged me >> Bible:Job 27:2]]." The devil received authority and tested Job night and day — first through outward things, later through the body, then through friends. When the wife did not conquer him, three friends came — not enemies with plotting doctrines, but true words badly and out of season. Through them the devil planned to make Job speak against Providence, turn impious under toil, and grow weary under pain. The truly courageous man — after Eliphaz’s three dialogues and Sophar’s two, when they fell silent — answers after the Scripture-named preface. "[[The Lord lives, who has thus judged me, and the Almighty who has embittered my soul >> Bible:Job 27:2]]." I know from where
